name: Sprocket
text: Run weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching to flag duplicates and near-duplicates. This keeps the merge debt low by catching redundant prompts early, before they clutter the system. The trade-off is occasional false positives from identical phrasing in unrelated prompts, but the cost is lower than the cleanup burden of letting duplicates pile up.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn't just false positives, it's that exact string matching might not catch nuanced duplicates or synonyms, allowing redundant prompts to slip through. A better alternative could be using natural language processing to identify semantic duplicates, rather than just relying on exact string matching. This argument would be settled by testing both approaches with a sample dataset and comparing their accuracy in identifying actual duplicates.
